# Final Report

The report is one outcome line, preceded by a short preamble only when there is something to say. Preamble first, outcome line last.

**The outcome line is required.** It is exactly one of:

       No commit was attempted: {reason}.
       Commit failed: {reason}.
       Committed successfully.

**The preamble is conditional.** Include either of these only when it applies:

- **Repo changes you made.** One line each, saying what and why: file edits, files created/deleted/renamed, mode changes, `.gitignore` or git config edits, hook or dependency changes -- anything beyond the staging, commit, and push this mode already authorizes. Edits you made to satisfy a pre-commit hook belong here. When you did change something, reporting it is unconditional: report it even when it was small, obvious, and fully successful.
- **Substantial issues.** Anything that went wrong or needed a retry, even when the final outcome is green: a hook that rejected the commit, a failing formatter or linter, a push that needed a second attempt, warnings a careful reviewer would want to see. Skip routine, expected output.

When neither applies, the outcome line is the entire report. Do not write `none`, `no changes`, or any other placeholder for an item that does not apply, and do not mention the staging, commit, or push itself -- those are the happy path this mode already asked for, and reporting them spends user attention on what was expected all along.

Never include the commit hash. When more than one commit was made, say how many. If you are stopping to ask the user a question, ask it -- these lines are for a completed turn only.

# Safety Checks

Stop and warn if changes include:
- Secrets (`.env`, credentials, API keys, certs)
- Large binaries that look accidental
- Files that seem unrelated to the apparent intent

1: # Status line customization[link](#status-line-customization)
2: 
3: Define custom scripting configurations and format dynamic JSON state payloads to customize your TUI status line.
4: 
5: info
6: 
7: To toggle the status line on/off or configure it from the TUI, see the Status Line Command.
8: 
9: ## Overview[link](#overview)
10: 
11: The status line is positioned at the bottom of the TUI prompt panel. It provides at-a-glance context regarding active agent cycles, workspace environments, context token window usages, and background execution tasks.
12: 
13: ## Custom status line scripting[link](#custom-status-line-scripting)
14: 
15: For advanced terminal layouts or custom status bar displays, you can route active agent metadata into a custom script.
16: 
17: ### Configuration[link](#configuration)
18: 
19: Add a `statusLine` configuration block to your `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` file:
20: 
21: json
22: 
23: content\_copy
24: 
25: ```json
26: {
27:   "statusLine": {
28:     "type": "command",
29:     "command": "~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/statusline.sh"
30:   }
31: }
32: ```
33: 
34: Whenever the agent state changes, the TUI executes your command script, pipes a detailed state JSON payload directly to the script’s `stdin`, reads your formatted string from `stdout`, and renders the result in the prompt’s status line. Full ANSI color codes are supported.
35: 
36: The block accepts three more optional keys: `padding` adds blank lines above the status line, `enabled` set to `false` suspends the script while keeping the command on file, and `stack_with_default` set to `true` renders your script below the built-in line instead of replacing it.
37: 
38: ### Available JSON fields[link](#available-json-fields)
39: 
40: The JSON payload piped to your script contains the following top-level fields:
41: 
42: Field Type Description `cwd` string Current working directory when the CLI was launched. `session_id` string Backward-compatibility alias for `conversation_id`. `conversation_id` string Current unique conversation ID. `transcript_path` string Absolute path to the active conversation transcript log file (optional). `model` object Contains `id` and `display_name` of the active model. `workspace` object Contains `current_dir` and `project_dir` paths. `version` string CLI version string. `context_window` object Contains token usage details: `total_input_tokens`, `total_output_tokens`, `context_window_size`, `used_percentage`, `remaining_percentage`, and `current_usage` sub-object. `exceeds_200k_tokens` bool True if the conversation context has exceeded 200k tokens (null before first API call). `product` string Application name (e.g., `antigravity`). `quota` object Maps model/bucket IDs to their quota status, containing `remaining_fraction`, `reset_time`, and `reset_in_seconds` (optional). `agent_state` string Current state: `idle`, `thinking`, `working`, `tool_use`, `initializing`. `vcs` object Version control info: `type` (git/jj/hg), `branch`, `client`, `dirty` (optional). `sandbox` object Sandbox configuration: `enabled`, `allow_network` (optional). `artifact_count` int Number of artifacts produced in the conversation. `plan_tier` string Subscription tier of the authenticated user (optional). `email` string Email/LDAP of the authenticated user. `pending_input_count` int Number of queued user messages. `tool_confirmation_pending` bool True when a tool confirmation dialog is showing. `task_count` int Number of running background tasks. `terminal_width` int Live width of the interactive terminal. `execution_mode` string Current active prompt execution mode (e.g., `planning`, `fast`). `vim` object Vim editing state: `mode` is `NORMAL`, `INSERT`, `VISUAL`, or `VISUAL LINE`. Present only when [Vim editor mode](/docs/cli/vim-editor-mode) is enabled.
43: 
44: ### JSON payload example[link](#json-payload-example)
45: 
46: Here is a fully sanitized, typical JSON payload piped to your status line script:
47: 
48: json
49: 
50: content\_copy
51: 
52: ```json
53: {
54:   "cwd": "/home/user/my-project",
55:   "session_id": "12345678-abcd-ef01-2345-6789abcdef01",
56:   "conversation_id": "12345678-abcd-ef01-2345-6789abcdef01",
57:   "transcript_path": "/home/user/.gemini/antigravity/brain/12345678-abcd-ef01-2345-6789abcdef01/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl",
58:   "model": {
59:     "id": "Gemini 3.5 Flash (High)",
60:     "display_name": "Gemini 3.5 Flash (High)"
61:   },
62:   "workspace": {
63:     "current_dir": "/home/user/my-project",
64:     "project_dir": "/home/user/my-project"
65:   },
66:   "version": "1.0.13",
67:   "context_window": {
68:     "total_input_tokens": 88244,
69:     "total_output_tokens": 61074,
70:     "context_window_size": 1048576,
71:     "used_percentage": 14.24,
72:     "remaining_percentage": 85.76,
73:     "current_usage": {
74:       "input_tokens": 63382,
75:       "output_tokens": 346,
76:       "cache_creation_input_tokens": 0,
77:       "cache_read_input_tokens": 20857
78:     }
79:   },
80:   "exceeds_200k_tokens": false,
81:   "product": "antigravity",
82:   "quota": {
83:     "gemini-weekly": {
84:       "remaining_fraction": 0.9378,
85:       "reset_time": "2026-07-06T07:50:32Z",
86:       "reset_in_seconds": 560580
87:     }
88:   },
89:   "agent_state": "idle",
90:   "vcs": {
91:     "type": "git",
92:     "branch": "main",
93:     "dirty": false
94:   },
95:   "sandbox": {
96:     "enabled": false
97:   },
98:   "artifact_count": 2,
99:   "plan_tier": "Pro",
100:   "email": "developer@email.com",
101:   "task_count": 1,
102:   "terminal_width": 111,
103:   "execution_mode": "planning"
104: }
105: ```
106: 
107: ### Example script[link](#example-script)
108: 
109: You can download a complete, layout-adaptive script from the official [statusline.sh example on GitHub](https://github.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli/blob/main/examples/statusline/statusline.sh). This script renders state badges, handles active branches, and formats context window progress bars dynamically.
110: 
111: Save the script to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/statusline.sh` and make it executable:
112: 
113: bash
114: 
115: content\_copy
116: 
117: ```bash
118: chmod +x ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/statusline.sh
119: ```

22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
23: #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
24: pub enum WorktreeOutside {
25:     Hide,
26:     Show,
27:     #[default]

29:     Directory,
30: }
31: 
32: impl WorktreeOutside {
33:     pub fn display_name(self) -> &'static str {
34:         match self {
35:             Self::Hide => "Hide",
36:             Self::Show => "Show",
37:             Self::Branch => "Branch",
38:             Self::Directory => "Directory",
39:         }
40:     }
41: 
42:     pub fn component_name(self) -> &'static str {
43:         match self {
44:             Self::Hide => "Worktree",
45:             Self::Show => "Worktree (Always Show)",
46:             Self::Branch => "Worktree (or Branch)",
47:             Self::Directory => "Worktree (or Directory)",
48:         }
49:     }
50: 
51:     pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
52:         match self {
53:             Self::Hide => "hide",
54:             Self::Show => "show",

389: pub enum AnsiColor {
390:     Color16 { c16: u8 },
391:     Color256 { c256: u8 },
392:     Rgb { r: u8, g: u8, b: u8 },
393: }
394: 
395: impl PartialEq for AnsiColor {
396:     fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
397:         match (self, other) {
398:             (AnsiColor::Color16 { c16: a }, AnsiColor::Color16 { c16: b }) => a == b,
399:             (AnsiColor::Color256 { c256: a }, AnsiColor::Color256 { c256: b }) => a == b,
400:             (
401:                 AnsiColor::Rgb {
402:                     r: r1,
403:                     g: g1,
404:                     b: b1,
405:                 },
406:                 AnsiColor::Rgb {
407:                     r: r2,
408:                     g: g2,
409:                     b: b2,
410:                 },
411:             ) => r1 == r2 && g1 == g2 && b1 == b2,
412:             _ => false,
413:         }
414:     }
415: }
416: 
417: impl Eq for AnsiColor {}
418: 
419: impl fmt::Display for AnsiColor {
420:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
421:         match self {
422:             AnsiColor::Color16 { c16 } => write!(f, "c16({})", c16),
423:             AnsiColor::Color256 { c256 } => write!(f, "c256({})", c256),
424:             AnsiColor::Rgb { r, g, b } => write!(f, "#{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}", r, g, b),
425:         }
426:     }

153: 
154:     let mut written = 0;
155:     for spec in &specs {
156:         let path = dir.join(format!("{}.toml", spec.name));
157:         if !force && path.exists() {
158:             continue;
159:         }
160: 
161:         let mut theme = UserTheme::default_theme();
162:         theme.active = spec.active;
163:         theme.style.mode = spec.mode;
164: 
165:         if let Some(colors) = color_schemes::find(spec.colors) {
166:             colors.apply_to(&mut theme.components);
167:         }
168:         if let Some(icons) = icon_sets::find(spec.icons) {
169:             icons.apply_to(&mut theme.components);
170:         }
171: 
172:         save_theme(&path, &theme)?;
173:         written += 1;
174:     }
175: 
176:     Ok(written)
177: }
178: 
179: /// List all .toml theme files in the themes directory.
180: /// Returns (name, path) pairs sorted by name.
181: pub fn list_themes() -> std::io::Result<Vec<(String, PathBuf)>> {
182:     let dir = themes_dir();
183:     list_theme_files(&dir)
184: }
185: 
186: fn list_theme_files(dir: &Path) -> std::io::Result<Vec<(String, PathBuf)>> {
187:     if !dir.exists() {
188:         return Ok(Vec::new());
189:     }
190:     let mut themes = Vec::new();
191:     for entry in fs::read_dir(dir)? {
192:         let entry = entry?;
193:         let path = entry.path();
194:         if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) == Some("toml")
195:             && let Some(name) = path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str())
196:         {
197:             themes.push((name.to_string(), path));
198:         }
199:     }
200:     themes.sort_by_key(|(name, _)| name.to_lowercase());
201:     Ok(themes)
202: }
203: 
204: /// Load a theme from a .toml file.
205: pub fn load_theme(path: &Path) -> Result<UserTheme, LoadError> {
206:     let content = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(LoadError::Io)?;
207:     let mut theme: UserTheme = toml::from_str(&content).map_err(LoadError::Parse)?;
208:     theme.add_missing_components();
209:     Ok(theme)
210: }
211: 
212: /// Save a theme to a .toml file.
213: pub fn save_theme(path: &Path, theme: &UserTheme) -> std::io::Result<()> {
214:     let content = toml::to_string_pretty(theme).map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;
215:     fs::write(path, content)
216: }
217: 
218: /// Find and load the active theme (first file with active=true).
219: /// If multiple are active, deactivates extras. If none active, activates the first.
220: pub fn load_active_theme() -> Result<(String, PathBuf, UserTheme), LoadError> {
221:     let dir = themes_dir();
222:     let themes = list_theme_files(&dir).map_err(LoadError::Io)?;
223: 
224:     if themes.is_empty() {
225:         return Err(LoadError::NoThemes);
226:     }
227: 
228:     let mut active: Option<(String, PathBuf, UserTheme)> = None;
229:     let mut extras_to_deactivate = Vec::new();
230: 
231:     for (name, path) in &themes {
232:         let theme = load_theme(path)?;
233:         if theme.active {
234:             if active.is_some() {
235:                 extras_to_deactivate.push(path.clone());
236:             } else {
237:                 active = Some((name.clone(), path.clone(), theme));
238:             }
239:         }
240:     }
241: 
242:     // Deactivate extras
243:     for path in extras_to_deactivate {
244:         if let Ok(mut theme) = load_theme(&path) {
245:             theme.active = false;
246:             let _ = save_theme(&path, &theme);
247:         }
248:     }
249: 
250:     // If none were active, activate the first
251:     if active.is_none() {
252:         let (name, path) = &themes[0];
253:         let mut theme = load_theme(path)?;
254:         theme.active = true;
255:         save_theme(path, &theme).map_err(LoadError::Io)?;
256:         active = Some((name.clone(), path.clone(), theme));
257:     }
258: 
259:     Ok(active.unwrap())
260: }
261: 
262: /// Activate a specific theme by name. Deactivates all others.
263: pub fn activate_theme(name: &str) -> Result<(), LoadError> {
264:     let dir = themes_dir();
265:     let themes = list_theme_files(&dir).map_err(LoadError::Io)?;
266: 
267:     let mut found = false;
268:     for (tname, path) in &themes {
269:         let mut theme = load_theme(path)?;
270:         let should_be_active = tname == name;
271:         if should_be_active {
272:             found = true;
273:         }
274:         if theme.active != should_be_active {
275:             theme.active = should_be_active;
276:             save_theme(path, &theme).map_err(LoadError::Io)?;
277:         }
278:     }
279: 
280:     if !found {
281:         return Err(LoadError::NotFound(name.to_string()));
282:     }
283:     Ok(())
284: }
285: 
286: /// Delete a theme file. Returns error if it's the last theme.
287: pub fn delete_theme(path: &Path) -> Result<(), DeleteError> {
288:     let dir = themes_dir();
289:     let themes = list_theme_files(&dir).map_err(DeleteError::Io)?;
290:     if themes.len() <= 1 {
291:         return Err(DeleteError::LastTheme);
292:     }
293:     fs::remove_file(path).map_err(DeleteError::Io)
294: }
295: 
296: /// Rename a theme file. Returns the new path.
297: pub fn rename_theme(old_path: &Path, new_name: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, RenameError> {
298:     if !is_valid_theme_name(new_name) {
299:         return Err(RenameError::InvalidName(new_name.to_string()));
300:     }
301: 
302:     let dir = old_path
303:         .parent()
304:         .ok_or_else(|| RenameError::InvalidName("no parent directory".into()))?;
305:     let new_path = dir.join(format!("{}.toml", new_name));
306: 
307:     if new_path.exists() {
308:         return Err(RenameError::AlreadyExists(new_name.to_string()));
309:     }
310: 
311:     fs::rename(old_path, &new_path).map_err(RenameError::Io)?;
312:     Ok(new_path)
313: }
314: 
315: /// Duplicate a theme. Returns the new path.
316: pub fn duplicate_theme(src_path: &Path, new_name: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, RenameError> {
317:     if !is_valid_theme_name(new_name) {
318:         return Err(RenameError::InvalidName(new_name.to_string()));
319:     }
320: 
321:     let dir = src_path
322:         .parent()
323:         .ok_or_else(|| RenameError::InvalidName("no parent directory".into()))?;
324:     let new_path = dir.join(format!("{}.toml", new_name));
325: 
326:     if new_path.exists() {
327:         return Err(RenameError::AlreadyExists(new_name.to_string()));
328:     }
329: 
330:     let mut theme = load_theme(src_path).map_err(|e| match e {
331:         LoadError::Io(io) => RenameError::Io(io),
332:         other => RenameError::Io(std::io::Error::other(format!("{}", other))),
333:     })?;
334:     theme.active = false; // duplicate is not active by default
335:     save_theme(&new_path, &theme).map_err(RenameError::Io)?;
336:     Ok(new_path)
337: }
338: 
339: /// Check if a theme name is valid for use as a filename on Windows/macOS/Linux.
340: pub fn is_valid_theme_name(name: &str) -> bool {
341:     if name.is_empty() || name.len() > 200 {
342:         return false;
343:     }
344: 
345:     // No path separators or null bytes
346:     if name.contains('/') || name.contains('\\') || name.contains('\0') {
347:         return false;
348:     }
349: 
350:     // No characters forbidden on Windows
351:     const FORBIDDEN: &[char] = &['<', '>', ':', '"', '|', '?', '*'];
352:     if name
353:         .chars()
354:         .any(|c| FORBIDDEN.contains(&c) || c.is_control())
355:     {
356:         return false;
357:     }
358: 
359:     // No leading/trailing spaces or dots (Windows issue)
360:     if name.starts_with(' ') || name.ends_with(' ') || name.starts_with('.') || name.ends_with('.')
361:     {
362:         return false;
363:     }
364: 
365:     // No reserved Windows names
366:     let upper = name.to_uppercase();
367:     const RESERVED: &[&str] = &[
368:         "CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL", "COM1", "COM2", "COM3", "COM4", "COM5", "COM6", "COM7", "COM8",
369:         "COM9", "LPT1", "LPT2", "LPT3", "LPT4", "LPT5", "LPT6", "LPT7", "LPT8", "LPT9",
370:     ];
371:     if RESERVED.contains(&upper.as_str()) {
372:         return false;
373:     }
374: 
375:     true
376: }
377: 
378: /// Get the path for a theme by name.
379: pub fn theme_path(name: &str) -> PathBuf {
380:     themes_dir().join(format!("{}.toml", name))
381: }

388:     Parse(toml::de::Error),
389:     NoThemes,
390:     NotFound(String),

394:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
395:         match self {
396:             LoadError::Io(e) => write!(f, "IO error: {}", e),
397:             LoadError::Parse(e) => write!(f, "parse error: {}", e),
398:             LoadError::NoThemes => write!(f, "no themes found"),
399:             LoadError::NotFound(name) => write!(f, "theme not found: {}", name),
400:         }
401:     }
402: }

256: /// Full demo text adjusted for component-specific display options.
257: pub fn demo_texts_for_components(
258:     components: &[ComponentConfig],
259: ) -> HashMap<ComponentId, SegmentText> {
260:     let mut texts = demo_texts_full();
261: 
262:     for (id, label, used) in [
263:         (ComponentId::UsageFiveHour, "5h", 23.0),
264:         (ComponentId::UsageSevenDay, "7d", 41.0),
265:     ] {
266:         let Some(usage) = components.iter().find(|component| component.id == id) else {
267:             continue;
268:         };
269:         let percentage = UsageValue::from_options(&usage.options).apply(used);
270:         texts.insert(id, (format!("{label} {percentage:.0}%"), String::new()));
271:     }
272: 
273:     let mut worktree_displays_branch = false;
274:     if let Some(worktree) = components
275:         .iter()
276:         .find(|component| component.id == ComponentId::Worktree)
277:     {
278:         match WorktreeOutside::from_options(&worktree.options) {
279:             WorktreeOutside::Hide => {
280:                 texts.remove(&ComponentId::Worktree);
281:             }
282:             WorktreeOutside::Show => {
283:                 texts.insert(ComponentId::Worktree, ("-".into(), String::new()));
284:             }
285:             WorktreeOutside::Branch => {
286:                 texts.insert(ComponentId::Worktree, ("main".into(), String::new()));
287:                 worktree_displays_branch = worktree.enabled;
288:             }
289:             WorktreeOutside::Directory => {
290:                 texts.insert(ComponentId::Worktree, ("project".into(), String::new()));
291:             }
292:         }
293:     }
294: 
295:     let git_autohides_branch = components
296:         .iter()
297:         .find(|component| component.id == ComponentId::Git)
298:         .is_some_and(|git| {
299:             git.options
300:                 .get(GIT_OPTION_AUTOHIDE_BRANCH)
301:                 .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
302:                 .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_GIT_AUTOHIDE_BRANCH)
303:         });
304:     if worktree_displays_branch
305:         && git_autohides_branch
306:         && let Some((primary, secondary)) = texts.get_mut(&ComponentId::Git)
307:         && primary == "main"
308:     {
309:         *primary = std::mem::take(secondary);
310:     }
311: 
312:     let Some(pull_request) = components
313:         .iter()
314:         .find(|component| component.id == ComponentId::PullRequest)
315:     else {
316:         return texts;
317:     };
318: 
319:     let show_review_state = pull_request
320:         .options
321:         .get(PR_OPTION_SHOW_REVIEW_STATE)
322:         .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
323:         .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_PR_SHOW_REVIEW_STATE);
324:     let show_url = pull_request
325:         .options
326:         .get(PR_OPTION_SHOW_URL)

34:         let mut out = String::with_capacity(display_name.len());
35:         let mut rest = display_name;
36: 
37:         while let Some(start) = rest.find('(') {
38:             out.push_str(&rest[..start]);
39:             let after_open = &rest[start + 1..];
40: 
41:             if let Some(end) = after_open.find(" context)") {
42:                 let token = &after_open[..end];
43:                 if !token.is_empty() && !token.chars().any(char::is_whitespace) {
44:                     out.push_str(token);
45:                     rest = &after_open[end + " context)".len()..];
46:                     continue;
47:                 }
48:             }
49: 
50:             out.push('(');
51:             rest = after_open;
52:         }
53: 
54:         out.push_str(rest);
55:         out
56:     }

34:     fn is_git_repository(dir: &str) -> bool {
35:         Command::new("git")
36:             .args(["--no-optional-locks", "rev-parse", "--git-dir"])
37:             .current_dir(dir)
38:             .output()
39:             .map(|o| o.status.success())
40:             .unwrap_or(false)
41:     }
42: 
43:     fn get_branch(dir: &str) -> Option<String> {
44:         let try_cmd = |args: &[&str]| -> Option<String> {
45:             let output = Command::new("git")
46:                 .args(args)
47:                 .current_dir(dir)
48:                 .output()
49:                 .ok()?;
50:             if output.status.success() {
51:                 let s = String::from_utf8(output.stdout).ok()?.trim().to_string();
52:                 if !s.is_empty() { Some(s) } else { None }
53:             } else {
54:                 None
55:             }
56:         };
57: 
58:         try_cmd(&["--no-optional-locks", "branch", "--show-current"])
59:             .or_else(|| try_cmd(&["--no-optional-locks", "symbolic-ref", "--short", "HEAD"]))
60:     }
61: 
62:     pub(crate) fn branch_name(dir: &str) -> Option<String> {
63:         if !Self::is_git_repository(dir) {
64:             return None;
65:         }
66: 
67:         Some(Self::get_branch(dir).unwrap_or_else(|| "detached".into()))
68:     }
69: 
70:     fn get_status(dir: &str) -> GitStatus {
71:         let output = Command::new("git")
72:             .args(["--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain"])
73:             .current_dir(dir)
74:             .output();
75: 
76:         match output {
77:             Ok(o) if o.status.success() => {
78:                 let text = String::from_utf8(o.stdout).unwrap_or_default();
79:                 if text.trim().is_empty() {
80:                     GitStatus::Clean
81:                 } else if text.contains("UU") || text.contains("AA") || text.contains("DD") {
82:                     GitStatus::Conflicts
83:                 } else {
84:                     GitStatus::Dirty
85:                 }
86:             }
87:             _ => GitStatus::Clean,
88:         }
89:     }
90: 
91:     fn get_commit_count(dir: &str, range: &str) -> u32 {
92:         Command::new("git")
93:             .args(["--no-optional-locks", "rev-list", "--count", range])
94:             .current_dir(dir)
95:             .output()
96:             .ok()
97:             .and_then(|o| {
98:                 if o.status.success() {
99:                     String::from_utf8(o.stdout).ok()?.trim().parse().ok()
100:                 } else {
101:                     None
102:                 }
103:             })
104:             .unwrap_or(0)
105:     }
106: 
107:     fn get_sha(dir: &str) -> Option<String> {
108:         let output = Command::new("git")
109:             .args(["--no-optional-locks", "rev-parse", "--short=7", "HEAD"])
110:             .current_dir(dir)
111:             .output()
112:             .ok()?;
113: 
114:         if output.status.success() {
115:             let sha = String::from_utf8(output.stdout).ok()?.trim().to_string();
116:             if sha.is_empty() { None } else { Some(sha) }
117:         } else {
118:             None
119:         }
120:     }
121: }
122:

125:         let dir = &input.workspace.current_dir;
126:         let branch = Self::branch_name(dir)?;
127:         let status = Self::get_status(dir);
128:         let ahead = Self::get_commit_count(dir, "@{u}..HEAD");

140:         metadata.insert("behind".into(), behind.to_string());

143:         }

148:             GitStatus::Dirty => status_parts.push("\u{25cf}".into()),
149:             GitStatus::Conflicts => status_parts.push("\u{26a0}".into()),
150:         }

152:             status_parts.push(format!("\u{2191}{}", ahead));
153:         }
154:         if behind > 0 {
155:             status_parts.push(format!("\u{2193}{}", behind));
156:         }
157:         if let Some(ref s) = sha {
158:             status_parts.push(s.clone());
159:         }
160: 
161:         Some(ComponentData {
162:             primary: branch,
163:             secondary: status_parts.join(" "),

165:         })

94:                 HostnameComponent::new().with_rstrip(rstrip).collect(input)
95:             }
96:             ComponentId::Git => {
97:                 let show_sha = comp_cfg
98:                     .options
99:                     .get("show_sha")
100:                     .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
101:                     .unwrap_or(false);
102:                 GitComponent::new().with_sha(show_sha).collect(input)
103:             }
104:             ComponentId::PullRequest => {
105:                 let show_review_state = comp_cfg
106:                     .options
107:                     .get(PR_OPTION_SHOW_REVIEW_STATE)
108:                     .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
109:                     .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_PR_SHOW_REVIEW_STATE);
110:                 let show_url = comp_cfg
111:                     .options
112:                     .get(PR_OPTION_SHOW_URL)
113:                     .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
114:                     .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_PR_SHOW_URL);
115:                 let osc_hyperlinks = comp_cfg
116:                     .options
117:                     .get(PR_OPTION_OSC_HYPERLINKS)
118:                     .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
119:                     .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_PR_OSC_HYPERLINKS);
120:                 PullRequestComponent::new()
121:                     .with_review_state(show_review_state)
122:                     .with_url(show_url)
123:                     .with_osc_hyperlinks(osc_hyperlinks)
124:                     .collect(input)
125:             }
126:             ComponentId::ContextWindow => ContextWindowComponent::new().collect(input),
127:             ComponentId::UsageFiveHour => FiveHourUsageComponent::new()
128:                 .with_value(UsageValue::from_options(&comp_cfg.options))
129:                 .collect(input),
130:             ComponentId::UsageSevenDay => SevenDayUsageComponent::new()
131:                 .with_value(UsageValue::from_options(&comp_cfg.options))
132:                 .collect(input),
133:             ComponentId::Cost => CostComponent::new().collect(input),
134:             ComponentId::Session => SessionComponent::new().collect(input),
135:             ComponentId::OutputStyle => OutputStyleComponent::new().collect(input),
136:             ComponentId::Separator => unreachable!(),
137:         };
138: 
139:         if let Some(data) = data {
140:             results.push((comp_cfg.clone(), data));
141:         }
142:     }
143: 
144:     autohide_duplicate_git_branch(&mut results);
145:     results
146: }
147: 
148: fn autohide_duplicate_git_branch(components: &mut [(ComponentConfig, ComponentData)]) {
149:     let displayed_branches: Vec<String> = components
150:         .iter()
151:         .filter(|(config, _)| config.id != ComponentId::Git)
152:         .filter_map(|(_, data)| data.metadata.get(METADATA_DISPLAYED_BRANCH).cloned())
153:         .collect();
154: 
155:     let Some((config, data)) = components
156:         .iter_mut()
157:         .find(|(config, _)| config.id == ComponentId::Git)
158:     else {
159:         return;
160:     };
161:     let autohide = config
162:         .options
163:         .get(GIT_OPTION_AUTOHIDE_BRANCH)
164:         .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
165:         .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_GIT_AUTOHIDE_BRANCH);
166: 
167:     if autohide
168:         && displayed_branches
169:             .iter()
170:             .any(|branch| branch == &data.primary)
171:     {
172:         data.primary = std::mem::take(&mut data.secondary);
173:     }
174: }

23: fn config_dir_arg(args: &[String]) -> Result<Option<PathBuf>, &'static str> {
24:     let mut config_dir = None;
25:     let mut index = 0;
26: 
27:     while index < args.len() {
28:         if args[index] == "--config-dir" {
29:             let Some(value) = args.get(index + 1) else {
30:                 return Err(CONFIG_DIR_ERROR);
31:             };
32:             if value.is_empty() || value.starts_with('-') {
33:                 return Err(CONFIG_DIR_ERROR);
34:             }
35:             config_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(value));
36:             index += 2;
37:             continue;
38:         }
39: 
40:         if let Some(value) = args[index].strip_prefix("--config-dir=") {
41:             if value.is_empty() {
42:                 return Err(CONFIG_DIR_ERROR);
43:             }
44:             config_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(value));
45:         }
46: 
47:         index += 1;
48:     }
49: 
50:     Ok(config_dir)
51: }
52: 
53: fn main() {
54:     let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
55: 
56:     if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--help" || a == "-h") {
57:         print_help();
58:         return;
59:     }
60: 
61:     if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--version" || a == "-V") {
62:         println!("xline {}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
63:         return;
64:     }
65: 
66:     let config_dir = match config_dir_arg(&args) {
67:         Ok(path) => path,
68:         Err(message) => {
69:             eprintln!("xline: {message}");
70:             std::process::exit(2);
71:         }
72:     };
73:     if let Some(path) = config_dir {
74:         xline::config::manager::set_config_dir_override(path)
75:             .expect("config directory override was already set");
76:     }
77: 
78:     // Handle --install-themes
79:     if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--install-themes") {
80:         let dir = xline::config::manager::themes_dir();
81:         if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir) {
82:             eprintln!("xline: cannot create themes dir: {}", e);
83:             std::process::exit(1);
84:         }
85:         match xline::config::manager::write_default_themes(&dir, true) {
86:             Ok(n) => {
87:                 eprintln!(
88:                     "xline: installed {} default theme(s) to {}",
89:                     n,
90:                     dir.display()
91:                 );
92:             }
93:             Err(e) => {
94:                 eprintln!("xline: error installing themes: {}", e);
95:                 std::process::exit(1);
96:             }
97:         }
98:         return;
99:     }
100: 
101:     // Bootstrap: ensure themes dir exists with starter themes
102:     if let Err(e) = xline::config::manager::bootstrap() {
103:         eprintln!("xline: bootstrap error: {}", e);
104:         std::process::exit(1);
105:     }
106: 
107:     let stdin_is_terminal = io::stdin().is_terminal();
108: 
109:     if stdin_is_terminal {
110:         // No stdin data → launch TUI editor
111:         if let Err(e) = xline::tui::run() {
112:             eprintln!("xline: TUI error: {}", e);
113:             std::process::exit(1);
114:         }
115:     } else {
116:         // Stdin has data → statusline rendering mode
117:         run_statusline();
118:     }
119: }
120: 
121: fn run_statusline() {
122:     // Read JSON from stdin
123:     let mut input_str = String::new();
124:     if let Err(e) = io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut input_str) {
125:         eprintln!("xline: stdin read error: {}", e);
126:         std::process::exit(1);
127:     }
128: 
129:     let input: xline::core::input::InputData = match serde_json::from_str(&input_str) {
130:         Ok(data) => data,
131:         Err(e) => {
132:             eprintln!("xline: JSON parse error: {}", e);
133:             std::process::exit(1);
134:         }
135:     };
136: 
137:     // Load active theme
138:     let (_name, _path, theme) = match xline::config::manager::load_active_theme() {
139:         Ok(t) => t,
140:         Err(e) => {
141:             eprintln!("xline: theme load error: {}", e);
142:             std::process::exit(1);
143:         }
144:     };
145: 
146:     // Collect component data and render
147:     let components = xline::core::statusline::collect_all_components(&theme, &input);
148:     let generator = xline::core::statusline::StatusLineGenerator::new(&theme);
149:     let statusline = generator.generate(components);
150: 
151:     print!("{}\x1b[0m", statusline);
152: }

294:     /// Add components introduced after this theme was saved, preserving the
295:     /// theme's existing component order and placing additions in default order.
296:     pub fn add_missing_components(&mut self) {
297:         let defaults = Self::default_theme().components;
298: 
299:         for (index, default) in defaults.iter().enumerate() {
300:             if self.get_component(default.id).is_some() {
301:                 continue;
302:             }
303: 
304:             let insert_at = defaults[index + 1..]
305:                 .iter()
306:                 .find_map(|next| self.components.iter().position(|c| c.id == next.id))
307:                 .unwrap_or(self.components.len());
308:             let mut addition = default.clone();
309:             if addition.id == ComponentId::Worktree {
310:                 // Preserve the visible output of existing themes. Fresh themes
311:                 // enable Worktree instead of Git, but migration should not
312:                 // silently replace an existing theme's Git segment.
313:                 addition.enabled = false;
314:             }
315:             self.components.insert(insert_at, addition);
316:         }
317:     }

## 4. Model Knowledge
- **Antigravity Statusline JSON Contract**:
  - Antigravity CLI pipes state JSON to stdin of custom script/command (e.g. `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/statusline.sh`), which calls `agyline`.
  - Key Antigravity fields:
    - `agent_state`: `"idle"`, `"thinking"`, `"working"`, `"tool_use"`, `"initializing"`.
    - `vcs`: `{ "type": "git", "branch": "main", "dirty": false }`. When present, avoids running slow `git` subprocesses!
    - `quota`: `{ "gemini-weekly": { "remaining_fraction": 0.9378, "reset_time": "...", "reset_in_seconds": 560580 } }`.
    - `context_window`: contains tokens, percentages, and `current_usage`.
    - `task_count`: integer count of background tasks.
- **Theme Ordering & Component Invariants**:
  - Every color scheme in `src/presets/color_schemes/` (`default.rs`, `cometix.rs`, `gruvbox.rs`, `late.rs`, `minimal.rs`, `nord.rs`, `powerline_dark.rs`, `powerline_light.rs`, `rose_pine.rs`, `tokyo_night.rs`) is tested by `presets::tests::test_all_color_schemes_load` to verify that `scheme.get(*id).is_some()` for EVERY `ComponentId` in `ComponentId::ALL`.
  - Every icon set in `src/presets/icon_sets/` (`emoji.rs`, `late.rs`, `minimal.rs`, `nerd_font.rs`, `powerline.rs`) is tested by `presets::tests::test_all_icon_sets_load` to verify that `set.get(*id).is_some()` for EVERY `ComponentId` in `ComponentId::ALL`.
  - `Separator` must always be the last component in `ComponentId::ALL` and `UserTheme.components`.

470:     /// Add components introduced after this theme was saved, preserving the
471:     /// theme's existing component order and placing additions in default order.
472:     pub fn add_missing_components(&mut self) {
473:         let defaults = Self::default_theme().components;
474: 
475:         for (index, default) in defaults.iter().enumerate() {
476:             if self.get_component(default.id).is_some() {
477:                 continue;
478:             }
479: 
480:             let insert_at = defaults[index + 1..]
481:                 .iter()
482:                 .find_map(|next| self.components.iter().position(|c| c.id == next.id))
483:                 .unwrap_or(self.components.len());
484:             let mut addition = default.clone();
485:             if addition.id == ComponentId::Worktree {
486:                 // Preserve the visible output of existing themes. Fresh themes
487:                 // enable Worktree instead of Git, but migration should not
488:                 // silently replace an existing theme's Git segment.
489:                 addition.enabled = false;
490:             }
491:             self.components.insert(insert_at, addition);
492:         }
493:     }

9:     println!("USAGE:");

14:     println!("    -h, --help                Print this help message");
15:     println!("    -V, --version             Print version");
16:     println!("    --config-dir <path>       Use a different xline config directory");
17:     println!("    --install-themes          Install/reinstall default themes");
18:     println!();

20:     println!("    XLINE_CONFIG_DIR          Override the xline config directory");

23: fn config_dir_arg(args: &[String]) -> Result<Option<PathBuf>, &'static str> {
24:     let mut config_dir = None;
25:     let mut index = 0;
26: 
27:     while index < args.len() {
28:         if args[index] == "--config-dir" {
29:             let Some(value) = args.get(index + 1) else {
30:                 return Err(CONFIG_DIR_ERROR);
31:             };
32:             if value.is_empty() || value.starts_with('-') {
33:                 return Err(CONFIG_DIR_ERROR);
34:             }
35:             config_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(value));
36:             index += 2;
37:             continue;
38:         }
39: 
40:         if let Some(value) = args[index].strip_prefix("--config-dir=") {
41:             if value.is_empty() {
42:                 return Err(CONFIG_DIR_ERROR);
43:             }
44:             config_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(value));
45:         }
46: 
47:         index += 1;
48:     }
49: 
50:     Ok(config_dir)
51: }
52: 
53: fn main() {
54:     let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
55: 
56:     if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--help" || a == "-h") {
57:         print_help();
58:         return;
59:     }
60: 
61:     if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--version" || a == "-V") {
62:         println!("xline {}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
63:         return;
64:     }
65: 
66:     let config_dir = match config_dir_arg(&args) {
67:         Ok(path) => path,
68:         Err(message) => {
69:             eprintln!("xline: {message}");
70:             std::process::exit(2);
71:         }
72:     };
73:     if let Some(path) = config_dir {
74:         xline::config::manager::set_config_dir_override(path)
75:             .expect("config directory override was already set");
76:     }
77: 
78:     // Handle --install-themes
79:     if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--install-themes") {
80:         let dir = xline::config::manager::themes_dir();
81:         if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir) {
82:             eprintln!("xline: cannot create themes dir: {}", e);
83:             std::process::exit(1);
84:         }
85:         match xline::config::manager::write_default_themes(&dir, true) {
86:             Ok(n) => {
87:                 eprintln!(
88:                     "xline: installed {} default theme(s) to {}",
89:                     n,
90:                     dir.display()
91:                 );
92:             }
93:             Err(e) => {
94:                 eprintln!("xline: error installing themes: {}", e);
95:                 std::process::exit(1);
96:             }

2: `xline` is a small Rust Claude Code Statusline.
3: 
4: ## Features
5: - keyboard-driven TUI editor built with `ratatui`
6: - starter themes written automatically on first run
7: - plain, Nerd Font, emoji, and powerline-style rendering
8: - configurable components for model, directory, worktree, hostname, git, pull requests, native context-window usage, separate five-hour and seven-day Claude rate limits, cost, session, and output style
9: - worktree-aware identity display with configurable Hide, Show, Branch, or Directory behavior outside worktrees, plus an optional original-branch field
10: - fresh themes enable Worktree with the Branch fallback and leave the richer Git status component disabled
11: - Git Status shows branch, file-change and upstream state, and optional SHA; branch autohiding removes duplication with another visible branch field
12: - pull-request number display with optional review state, URL, and separate OSC 8 hyperlinks for every visible PR field
13: - configurable comma-separated suffix stripping for displayed hostnames
14: 
15: ## Build and Install
16: ```bash
17: # Build from source:
18: cargo build --release
19: # install locally
20: cargo install --path .
21: ```
22:

24: Run `xline` in a terminal to open the theme editor:
25: ```bash
26: xline
27: ```
28: 
29: Add to Claude Code by editing ~/.claude/settings.json and adding/editing the top-level property:
30: ```json
31: "statusLine": {
32:   "type": "command",
33:   "command": "xline",
34:   "padding": 0
35: }
36: ```
37: 
38: ## Config Directory
39: By default, `xline` stores its configuration in `~/.claude/xline`, with themes
40: in the `themes` subdirectory. Override the config directory for one-off runs or
41: isolated testing with `--config-dir`:
42: ```bash
43: xline --config-dir /tmp/xline-test
44: ```
45: 
46: For shells, wrappers, and CI, set `XLINE_CONFIG_DIR`:
47: ```bash
48: XLINE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/xline-test xline
49: ```
50: 
51: The command-line option takes precedence over `XLINE_CONFIG_DIR`, which takes
52: precedence over the default. The selected directory applies to the TUI,
53: statusline rendering, initial theme bootstrap, and `--install-themes`.
54:

The following code has been modified to include a line number before every line, in the format: <line_number>: <original_line>. Please note that any changes targeting the original code should remove the line number, colon, and leading space.
1: # Status line customization[link](#status-line-customization)
2: 
3: Define custom scripting configurations and format dynamic JSON state payloads to customize your TUI status line.
4: 
5: info
6: 
7: To toggle the status line on/off or configure it from the TUI, see the Status Line Command.
8: 
9: ## Overview[link](#overview)
10: 
11: The status line is positioned at the bottom of the TUI prompt panel. It provides at-a-glance context regarding active agent cycles, workspace environments, context token window usages, and background execution tasks.
12: 
13: ## Custom status line scripting[link](#custom-status-line-scripting)
14: 
15: For advanced terminal layouts or custom status bar displays, you can route active agent metadata into a custom script.
16: 
17: ### Configuration[link](#configuration)
18: 
19: Add a `statusLine` configuration block to your `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` file:
20: 
21: json
22: 
23: content\_copy
24: 
25: ```json
26: {
27:   "statusLine": {
28:     "type": "command",
29:     "command": "~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/statusline.sh"
30:   }
31: }
32: ```
33: 
34: Whenever the agent state changes, the TUI executes your command script, pipes a detailed state JSON payload directly to the script’s `stdin`, reads your formatted string from `stdout`, and renders the result in the prompt’s status line. Full ANSI color codes are supported.
35: 
36: The block accepts three more optional keys: `padding` adds blank lines above the status line, `enabled` set to `false` suspends the script while keeping the command on file, and `stack_with_default` set to `true` renders your script below the built-in line instead of replacing it.
37: 
38: ### Available JSON fields[link](#available-json-fields)
39: 
40: The JSON payload piped to your script contains the following top-level fields:
41: 
42: Field Type Description `cwd` string Current working directory when the CLI was launched. `session_id` string Backward-compatibility alias for `conversation_id`. `conversation_id` string Current unique conversation ID. `transcript_path` string Absolute path to the active conversation transcript log file (optional). `model` object Contains `id` and `display_name` of the active model. `workspace` object Contains `current_dir` and `project_dir` paths. `version` string CLI version string. `context_window` object Contains token usage details: `total_input_tokens`, `total_output_tokens`, `context_window_size`, `used_percentage`, `remaining_percentage`, and `current_usage` sub-object. `exceeds_200k_tokens` bool True if the conversation context has exceeded 200k tokens (null before first API call). `product` string Application name (e.g., `antigravity`). `quota` object Maps model/bucket IDs to their quota status, containing `remaining_fraction`, `reset_time`, and `reset_in_seconds` (optional). `agent_state` string Current state: `idle`, `thinking`, `working`, `tool_use`, `initializing`. `vcs` object Version control info: `type` (git/jj/hg), `branch`, `client`, `dirty` (optional). `sandbox` object Sandbox configuration: `enabled`, `allow_network` (optional). `artifact_count` int Number of artifacts produced in the conversation. `plan_tier` string Subscription tier of the authenticated user (optional). `email` string Email/LDAP of the authenticated user. `pending_input_count` int Number of queued user messages. `tool_confirmation_pending` bool True when a tool confirmation dialog is showing. `task_count` int Number of running background tasks. `terminal_width` int Live width of the interactive terminal. `execution_mode` string Current active prompt execution mode (e.g., `planning`, `fast`). `vim` object Vim editing state: `mode` is `NORMAL`, `INSERT`, `VISUAL`, or `VISUAL LINE`. Present only when [Vim editor mode](/docs/cli/vim-editor-mode) is enabled.

+// --- Antigravity CLI statusLine configuration ---
+
+#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum AgySetupResult {
+    Configured { path: PathBuf, already_set: bool },
+    Conflict { path: PathBuf, existing_command: String },
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum AgyUnsetupResult {
+    Removed { path: PathBuf },
+    NotConfigured { path: PathBuf },
+    DifferentCommand { path: PathBuf, existing_command: String },
+}
+
+/// Configure Antigravity CLI settings.json to use `agyline` as the statusline provider.
+pub fn setup_agy_statusline(settings_path: &Path, force: bool) -> Result<AgySetupResult, String> {
+    let mut root: serde_json::Value = if settings_path.exists() {
+        let content = fs::read_to_string(settings_path)
+            .map_err(|e| format!("failed to read {}: {}", settings_path.display(), e))?;
+        if content.trim().is_empty() {
+            serde_json::json!({})
+        } else {
+            serde_json::from_str(&content)
+                .map_err(|e| format!("failed to parse {}: {}", settings_path.display(), e))?
+        }
+    } else {
+        serde_json::json!({})
+    };
+
+    let obj = root.as_object_mut().ok_or_else(|| {
+        format!("root JSON in {} must be an object", settings_path.display())
+    })?;
+
+    if let Some(existing_sl) = obj.get("statusLine") {
+        if let Some(sl_obj) = existing_sl.as_object() {
+            let cmd = sl_obj.get("command").and_then(|c| c.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
+            if cmd == "agyline" {
+                let sl_type = sl_obj.get("type").and_then(|t| t.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
+                if sl_type == "command" {
+                    return Ok(AgySetupResult::Configured {
+                        path: settings_path.to_path_buf(),
+                        already_set: true,
+                    });
+                }
+            } else if !cmd.is_empty() && !force {
+                return Ok(AgySetupResult::Conflict {
+                    path: settings_path.to_path_buf(),
+                    existing_command: cmd.to_string(),
+                });
+            }
+        } else if !force {
+            return Ok(AgySetupResult::Conflict {
+                path: settings_path.to_path_buf(),
+                existing_command: existing_sl.to_string(),
+            });
+        }
+    }
+
+    // Insert or update statusLine
+    let status_line = serde_json::json!({
+        "type": "command",
+        "command": "agyline"
+    });
+    obj.insert("statusLine".to_string(), status_line);
+
+    if let Some(parent) = settings_path.parent() {
+        fs::create_dir_all(parent)
+            .map_err(|e| format!("failed to create directory {}: {}", parent.display(), e))?;
+    }
+
+    let serialized = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&root)
+        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to serialize JSON: {}", e))?;
+    fs::write(settings_path, format!("{}\n", serialized))
+        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to write {}: {}", settings_path.display(), e))?;
+
+    Ok(AgySetupResult::Configured {
+        path: settings_path.to_path_buf(),
+        already_set: false,
+    })
+}
+
+/// Remove `agyline` statusline configuration from Antigravity CLI settings.json.
+pub fn unsetup_agy_statusline(settings_path: &Path) -> Result<AgyUnsetupResult, String> {
+    if !settings_path.exists() {
+        return Ok(AgyUnsetupResult::NotConfigured {
+            path: settings_path.to_path_buf(),
+        });
+    }
+
+    let content = fs::read_to_string(settings_path)
+        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to read {}: {}", settings_path.display(), e))?;
+    if content.trim().is_empty() {
+        return Ok(AgyUnsetupResult::NotConfigured {
+            path: settings_path.to_path_buf(),
+        });
+    }
+
+    let mut root: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&content)
+        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to parse {}: {}", settings_path.display(), e))?;
+
+    let obj = root.as_object_mut().ok_or_else(|| {
+        format!("root JSON in {} must be an object", settings_path.display())
+    })?;
+
+    let Some(existing_sl) = obj.get("statusLine") else {
+        return Ok(AgyUnsetupResult::NotConfigured {
+            path: settings_path.to_path_buf(),
+        });
+    };
+
+    if let Some(sl_obj) = existing_sl.as_object() {
+        let cmd = sl_obj.get("command").and_then(|c| c.as_str()).unwrap_or("");
+        if cmd != "agyline" {
+            return Ok(AgyUnsetupResult::DifferentCommand {
+                path: settings_path.to_path_buf(),
+                existing_command: cmd.to_string(),
+            });
+        }
+    }
+
+    obj.remove("statusLine");
+
+    let serialized = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&root)
+        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to serialize JSON: {}", e))?;
+    fs::write(settings_path, format!("{}\n", serialized))
+        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to write {}: {}", settings_path.display(), e))?;
+
+    Ok(AgyUnsetupResult::Removed {
+        path: settings_path.to_path_buf(),
+    })
+}

+        let settings_path = dir.path().join("settings.json");
+        fs::write(

+            r#"{"statusLine": {"type": "command", "command": "custom-status.sh"}}"#,

The following code has been modified to include a line number before every line, in the format: <line_number>: <original_line>. Please note that any changes targeting the original code should remove the line number, colon, and leading space.
1: # agyline
2: `agyline` is a fast, customizable statusline generator and interactive TUI theme editor for the Google Antigravity CLI (and compatible AI coding assistants).
3: 
4: ## Features
5: - **Keyboard-driven TUI editor** built with `ratatui`
6: - **Official Google Antigravity support**: Built-in support for `agent_state`, `model`, `vcs` (git), `context_window`, `quota` (weekly bucket), `task_count`, `execution_mode`, `vim`, `artifact_count`, `sandbox`, `plan_tier`, `email`, and more.
7: - **Smart model tier icons**: Gemini model tiers (`Flash`, `Pro`, `Ultra`, `Flash Lite`) with customizable icons, preserving Claude model tiers (`Opus`, `Sonnet`, `Haiku`).
8: - **Fast native VCS handling**: Utilizes precomputed `vcs` payload from Antigravity to avoid slow subprocess calls.
9: - **Rich preset collection**: 10 built-in color schemes (Default, Cometix, Gruvbox, Late, Minimal, Nord, Powerline Dark, Powerline Light, Rose Pine, Tokyo Night) and 5 icon sets (Emoji, Late, Minimal, Nerd Font, Powerline).
10: - **Multiple rendering styles**: Plain, Nerd Font, Emoji, and Powerline glyph modes.
11: 
12: ## Build and Install
13: ```bash
14: # Build from source:
15: cargo build --release
16: 
17: # Install locally:
18: cargo install --path .
19: ```
20: 
21: ## Usage
22: Run `agyline` in a terminal to launch the interactive theme editor:
23: ```bash
24: agyline
25: ```
26: 
27: ### Configure in Google Antigravity CLI
28: Create a statusline helper script, e.g. `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/statusline.sh`:
29: ```bash
30: #!/usr/bin/env bash
31: # Read Antigravity CLI JSON from stdin and pipe to agyline
32: exec agyline
33: ```
34: Make it executable:
35: ```bash
36: chmod +x ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/statusline.sh
37: ```
38: 
39: Then configure the statusline command in Antigravity or invoke `agyline` directly with JSON on stdin.
40: 
41: ## Config Directory
42: By default, `agyline` stores its configuration in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/agyline` (with fallback to `XLINE_CONFIG_DIR`). Override the config directory with `--config-dir`:
43: ```bash
44: agyline --config-dir /tmp/agyline-test
45: ```
46: 
47: Or via environment variable:
48: ```bash
49: AGYLINE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/agyline-test agyline
50: ```
51: 
52: ## Inspiration
53: This project drew inspiration from [CCometixLine](https://github.com/Haleclipse/CCometixLine).
54: 
55:

+```bash
+# Configure statusLine in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json

29: fn config_dir_arg(args: &[String]) -> Result<Option<PathBuf>, &'static str> {
30:     let mut config_dir = None;
31:     let mut index = 0;
32: 
33:     while index < args.len() {
34:         if args[index] == "--config-dir" {
35:             let Some(value) = args.get(index + 1) else {
36:                 return Err(CONFIG_DIR_ERROR);
37:             };
38:             if value.is_empty() || value.starts_with('-') {
39:                 return Err(CONFIG_DIR_ERROR);
40:             }
41:             config_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(value));
42:             index += 2;
43:             continue;
44:         }
45: 
46:         if let Some(value) = args[index].strip_prefix("--config-dir=") {
47:             if value.is_empty() {
48:                 return Err(CONFIG_DIR_ERROR);
49:             }
50:             config_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(value));
51:         }
52: 
53:         index += 1;
54:     }
55: 
56:     Ok(config_dir)
57: }

194: fn run_statusline() {
195:     // Read JSON from stdin
196:     let mut input_str = String::new();
197:     if let Err(e) = io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut input_str) {
198:         eprintln!("agyline: stdin read error: {}", e);
199:         std::process::exit(1);
200:     }
201: 
202:     let input: agyline::core::input::InputData = match serde_json::from_str(&input_str) {
203:         Ok(data) => data,
204:         Err(e) => {
205:             eprintln!("agyline: JSON parse error: {}", e);
206:             std::process::exit(1);
207:         }
208:     };
209: 
210:     // Load active theme
211:     let (_name, _path, theme) = match agyline::config::manager::load_active_theme() {
212:         Ok(t) => t,
213:         Err(e) => {
214:             eprintln!("agyline: theme load error: {}", e);
215:             std::process::exit(1);
216:         }
217:     };
218: 
219:     // Collect component data and render
220:     let components = agyline::core::statusline::collect_all_components(&theme, &input);
221:     let generator = agyline::core::statusline::StatusLineGenerator::new(&theme);
222:     let statusline = generator.generate(components);
223: 
224:     print!("{}\x1b[0m", statusline);
225: }

1: # agyline
2: `agyline` is a fast, customizable statusline generator and interactive TUI theme editor for the Google Antigravity CLI (and compatible AI coding assistants).
3: 
4: ## Features
5: - **Keyboard-driven TUI editor** built with `ratatui`
6: - **Official Google Antigravity support**: Built-in support for `agent_state`, `model`, `vcs` (git), `context_window`, `quota` (weekly bucket), `task_count`, `execution_mode`, `vim`, `artifact_count`, `sandbox`, `plan_tier`, `email`, and more.
7: - **Smart model tier icons**: Gemini model tiers (`Flash`, `Pro`, `Ultra`, `Flash Lite`) with customizable icons, preserving Claude model tiers (`Opus`, `Sonnet`, `Haiku`).
8: - **Fast native VCS handling**: Utilizes precomputed `vcs` payload from Antigravity to avoid slow subprocess calls.
9: - **Rich preset collection**: 10 built-in color schemes (Default, Cometix, Gruvbox, Late, Minimal, Nord, Powerline Dark, Powerline Light, Rose Pine, Tokyo Night) and 5 icon sets (Emoji, Late, Minimal, Nerd Font, Powerline).
10: - **Multiple rendering styles**: Plain, Nerd Font, Emoji, and Powerline glyph modes.
11: 
12: ## Build and Install
13: ```bash
14: # Build from source:
15: cargo build --release
16: 
17: # Install locally:
18: cargo install --path .
19: ```
20: 
21: ## Usage
22: Run `agyline` in a terminal to launch the interactive theme editor:
23: ```bash
24: agyline
25: ```
26: 
27: ### Automatic Setup with Google Antigravity CLI
28: Quickly configure Antigravity CLI to use `agyline`:
29: ```bash
30: # Configure statusLine in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json
31: agyline --agy-setup
32: 
33: # Overwrite if a different statusLine command is already configured
34: agyline --agy-setup-force
35: 
36: # Remove agyline from settings.json
37: agyline --agy-unsetup
38: ```
39: 
40: ### Manual Configuration
41: You can also manually edit `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`:
42: ```json
43: {
44:   "statusLine": {
45:     "type": "command",
46:     "command": "agyline"
47:   }
48: }
49: ```
50: 
51: ## Config Directory
52: By default, `agyline` stores its configuration in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/agyline` (with fallback to `XLINE_CONFIG_DIR`). Override the config directory with `--config-dir`:
53: ```bash
54: agyline --config-dir /tmp/agyline-test
55: ```
56: 
57: Or via environment variable:
58: ```bash
59: AGYLINE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/agyline-test agyline
60: ```

6. Report as described in the Final Report section below

# Final Report

The report is one outcome line, preceded by a short preamble only when there is something to say. Preamble first, outcome line last.

**The outcome line is required.** It is exactly one of:

       No commit was attempted: {reason}.
       Commit failed: {reason}.
       Committed and pushed successfully.
       Committed successfully, push not attempted: {reason}.
       Committed successfully, push failed:
       {reason}

**The preamble is conditional.** Include either of these only when it applies:

- **Repo changes you made.** One line each, saying what and why: file edits, files created/deleted/renamed, mode changes, `.gitignore` or git config edits, hook or dependency changes -- anything beyond the staging, commit, and push this mode already authorizes. Edits you made to satisfy a pre-commit hook belong here. When you did change something, reporting it is unconditional: report it even when it was small, obvious, and fully successful.
- **Substantial issues.** Anything that went wrong or needed a retry, even when the final outcome is green: a hook that rejected the commit, a failing formatter or linter, a push that needed a second attempt, warnings a careful reviewer would want to see. Skip routine, expected output.

When neither applies, the outcome line is the entire report. Do not write `none`, `no changes`, or any other placeholder for an item that does not apply, and do not mention the staging, commit, or push itself -- those are the happy path this mode already asked for, and reporting them spends user attention on what was expected all along.

Never include the commit hash. When more than one commit was made, say how many. When the push published earlier unpushed commits, say so on the outcome line. If you are stopping to ask the user a question, ask it -- these lines are for a completed turn only.

# Safety Checks

Stop and warn if changes include:
- Secrets (`.env`, credentials, API keys, certs)
- Large binaries that look accidental
- Files that seem unrelated to the apparent intent

+pub const LOG_FILE_ENV: &str = "AGYLINE_LOG_FILE";

+fn iso_timestamp_zulu() -> String {
+    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now();
+    let duration = now.duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default();
+    let total_secs = duration.as_secs();
+    let millis = duration.subsec_millis();
+
+    let days = total_secs / 86400;
+    let rem_secs = total_secs % 86400;
+    let hours = rem_secs / 3600;
+    let minutes = (rem_secs % 3600) / 60;
+    let seconds = rem_secs % 60;
+
+    let z = days as i64 + 719468;
+    let era = (if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146096 }) / 146097;
+    let doe = (z - era * 146097) as u64;
+    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146096) / 365;
+    let y = yoe as i64 + era * 400;
+    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
+    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
+    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
+    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
+    let year = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
+
+    format!(
+        "{:04}-{:02}-{:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}.{:03}Z",
+        year, m, d, hours, minutes, seconds, millis
+    )
+}
+
+fn log_payload_to_file(log_path: &str, raw_json: &str) {
+    use std::fs::OpenOptions;
+    use std::io::Write;
+    use std::path::Path;
+
+    let pretty_json = match serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(raw_json) {
+        Ok(val) => serde_json::to_string_pretty(&val).unwrap_or_else(|_| raw_json.trim().to_string()),
+        Err(_) => raw_json.trim().to_string(),
+    };
+
+    let timestamp = iso_timestamp_zulu();
+    let entry = format!("/* {} */\n{}\n\n", timestamp, pretty_json);
+
+    let path = Path::new(log_path);
+    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
+        let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(parent);
+    }
+
+    if let Ok(mut file) = OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(path) {
+        let _ = file.write_all(entry.as_bytes());
+    }
+}
+

assistant 2026-08-17 04:27:02
The reason you are seeing **`weekly 55%`** instead of **`5h`** is due to the difference between Claude Code and Google Antigravity's quota systems:

### Why `5h` is not showing
- **Claude Code** reports usage via a 5-hour sliding window (`rate_limits.five_hour`) and a 7-day window (`rate_limits.seven_day`).
- **Google Antigravity CLI** does not use 5-hour rate limit windows. Instead, Antigravity manages quotas on a **weekly bucket cycle**, provided in the stdin payload under:
  ```json
  "quota": {
    "gemini-weekly": {
      "remaining_fraction": 0.55,
      "reset_time": "...",
      "reset_in_seconds": ...
    }
  }
  ```

### What is currently showing
In your statusline image:
$$\text{⯈ Gemini 3.7 Flash (High) | 🤖 idle | 📁 agyline |  ✓ |  main | 🖴 22.1% · 405.0k tokens | }\mathbf{⌛\text{ weekly 55\%}}$$

- **`⌛ weekly 55%`** is Antigravity's active quota component (`QuotaComponent`), indicating **55% remaining** on your current weekly Gemini quota.
- The `5h` component (`UsageFiveHour`) stays hidden when connected to Antigravity because no `rate_limits.five_hour` object is provided in Antigravity's state payload.

38: fn collect_window(
39:     label: &str,
40:     window: Option<&RateLimitWindow>,
41:     value: UsageValue,
42: ) -> Option<ComponentData> {
43:     let window = window?;
44:     let percentage = window.used_percentage?;
45:     let displayed = value.apply(percentage);
46:     let value = if displayed.fract() == 0.0 {
47:         format!("{displayed:.0}")
48:     } else {
49:         format!("{displayed:.1}")
50:     };
51: 
52:     let mut metadata = HashMap::from([("percentage".into(), percentage.to_string())]);
53:     if let Some(resets_at) = window.resets_at {
54:         metadata.insert("resets_at".into(), resets_at.to_string());
55:     }
56: 
57:     Some(ComponentData {
58:         primary: format!("{label} {value}%"),
59:         secondary: String::new(),
60:         metadata,
61:     })
62: }
63: 
64: impl Component for FiveHourUsageComponent {
65:     fn collect(&self, input: &InputData) -> Option<ComponentData> {
66:         collect_window(
67:             "5h",
68:             input
69:                 .rate_limits
70:                 .as_ref()
71:                 .and_then(|limits| limits.five_hour.as_ref()),
72:             self.value,
73:         )
74:     }
75: 
76:     fn id(&self) -> ComponentId {
77:         ComponentId::UsageFiveHour
78:     }
79: }
80:

+fn collect_quota_window(
+    label: &str,
+    bucket: Option<&crate::core::input::QuotaBucket>,
+    value: UsageValue,
+) -> Option<ComponentData> {
+    let bucket = bucket?;
+    let fraction = bucket.remaining_fraction?;
+    let used_percentage = ((1.0 - fraction) * 100.0).clamp(0.0, 100.0);
+    let displayed = value.apply(used_percentage);
+    let value_str = if displayed.fract() == 0.0 {
+        format!("{displayed:.0}")
+    } else {
+        format!("{displayed:.1}")
+    };
+
+    let mut metadata = HashMap::from([("percentage".into(), used_percentage.to_string())]);
+    if let Some(reset_sec) = bucket.reset_in_seconds {
+        metadata.insert("reset_in_seconds".into(), reset_sec.to_string());
+    }
+
+    Some(ComponentData {
+        primary: format!("{label} {value_str}%"),
+        secondary: String::new(),
+        metadata,
+    })
+}

assistant 2026-08-17 04:28:23
Looking at [`/tmp/agyline.log`](file:///tmp/agyline.log), we can see the exact quota structure Antigravity CLI sends:

```json
"quota": {
  "gemini-5h": {
    "remaining_fraction": 0.9142425,
    "reset_in_seconds": 14549,
    "reset_time": "2026-08-17T08:23:39Z"
  },
  "gemini-weekly": {
    "remaining_fraction": 0.55474836,
    "reset_in_seconds": 259394,
    "reset_time": "2026-08-20T04:24:24Z"
  },
  "3p-5h": {
    "remaining_fraction": 1,
    "reset_in_seconds": 17990,
    "reset_time": "2026-08-17T09:21:00Z"
  },
  "3p-weekly": {
    "remaining_fraction": 0.6661629,
    "reset_in_seconds": 286557,
    "reset_time": "2026-08-20T11:57:07Z"
  }
}
```

### Why `5h` was missing
1. Antigravity places its 5-hour rate limit inside `"quota"."gemini-5h"` (and `"3p-5h"`).
2. Previously, `UsageFiveHour` (`5h`) only looked for Claude Code's `"rate_limits"."five_hour"` object and did not check Antigravity's `"quota"` buckets.

### What has been updated
- [`src/core/components/usage.rs`](file:///Users/mclark/p/my/agyline/src/core/components/usage.rs):
  - **`UsageFiveHour` (`5h`)**: Automatically extracts from `quota["gemini-5h"]` (or `"3p-5h"`).
  - **`UsageSevenDay` (`7d`)**: Automatically extracts from `quota["gemini-weekly"]` (or `"3p-weekly"`).
- Both components respect the configured `value` mode (`used` vs `remaining`).
- When `UsageFiveHour` is enabled in your theme, it will now display your 5-hour quota (`5h 91.4%` remaining / `5h 8.6%` used).

33:     fn format_display_name(display_name: &str) -> String {
34:         let mut out = String::with_capacity(display_name.len());
35:         let mut rest = display_name;
36: 
37:         while let Some(start) = rest.find('(') {
38:             out.push_str(&rest[..start]);
39:             let after_open = &rest[start + 1..];
40: 
41:             if let Some(end) = after_open.find(" context)") {
42:                 let token = &after_open[..end];
43:                 if !token.is_empty() && !token.chars().any(char::is_whitespace) {
44:                     out.push_str(token);
45:                     rest = &after_open[end + " context)".len()..];
46:                     continue;
47:                 }
48:             }
49: 
50:             out.push('(');
51:             rest = after_open;
52:         }
53: 
54:         out.push_str(rest);
55:         out
56:     }

## 4. Model Knowledge
- **Antigravity CLI Schema Details**:
  - `quota` object is a map `HashMap<String, QuotaBucket>` containing keys like `"gemini-5h"`, `"gemini-weekly"`, `"3p-5h"`, `"3p-weekly"`. Each contains `remaining_fraction: Option<f64>`, `reset_time: Option<String>`, and `reset_in_seconds: Option<u64>`.
  - `model` object has `id: String`, `display_name: String`, `effort: Option<String>` (e.g. `"high"`).
  - `workspace` has `current_dir: String` and `project_dir: Option<String>`.
- **Component Behaviors when Fields are Dropped**:
  - `FiveHourUsageComponent` & `SevenDayUsageComponent`: now exclusively rely on `input.quota`.
  - `ModelComponent`: reads effort from `input.model.effort`.
  - `SessionComponent`: reads session ID from `input.session_id` or `input.conversation_id`.
  - `WorktreeComponent`: operates on `workspace.current_dir` and `outside_worktrees` mode.
  - `PullRequestComponent`, `CostComponent`, `OutputStyleComponent`: return `None` on collect since Antigravity does not provide these fields.

user 2026-08-17 04:32:24
what's the difference between: gemini-5h, 3p-5h

assistant 2026-08-17 04:32:24
In Google Antigravity CLI, **`gemini-5h`** and **`3p-5h`** represent separate 5-hour rolling quota pools:

| Quota Bucket | Provider | Purpose | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`gemini-5h`** | **1st-Party (Google)** | 5-hour rate limit allowance for native Google Gemini models. | `Gemini 3.7 Flash`, `Gemini 3.5 Pro`, `Flash Lite`, `Ultra` |
| **`3p-5h`** | **3rd-Party ("3p")** | 5-hour rate limit allowance for external / non-Google models proxied through Antigravity. | `Claude 3.7 Sonnet`, `GPT-4o`, external LLM endpoints |

Similarly, Antigravity tracks corresponding weekly cycles for both:
- **`gemini-weekly`**: Google AI weekly quota pool.
- **`3p-weekly`**: 3rd-party weekly quota pool.

assistant 2026-08-17 04:33:49
Yes! `agyline` automatically selects between **`gemini-*`** and **`3p-*`** quota pools based on the active model:

### How Automatic Quota Switching Works

1. **Model Detection** ([`src/core/input.rs`](file:///Users/mclark/p/my/agyline/src/core/input.rs)):
   - Evaluates `input.model.id` and `input.model.display_name`.
   - If the active model is 3rd-party (e.g. `claude-3-7-sonnet`, `gpt-4o`, etc.), it recognizes the session as a 3rd-party model session.
   - If the model is a native Google model (e.g. `Gemini 3.7 Flash`, `Gemini Pro`, `Flash Lite`, `Ultra`), it recognizes it as a Gemini session.

2. **5-Hour Quota (`5h`)** ([`src/core/components/usage.rs`](file:///Users/mclark/p/my/agyline/src/core/components/usage.rs)):
   - **Active 3rd-Party Model**: Prioritizes `3p-5h` (e.g. `5h 100%`).
   - **Active Gemini Model**: Prioritizes `gemini-5h` (e.g. `5h 91.4%`).

3. **Weekly / 7-Day Quota (`7d` & `Quota`)** ([`src/core/components/quota.rs`](file:///Users/mclark/p/my/agyline/src/core/components/quota.rs)):
   - **Active 3rd-Party Model**: Selects `3p-weekly` (e.g. `3p-weekly 66.6%`).
   - **Active Gemini Model**: Selects `gemini-weekly` (e.g. `weekly 55.4%`).

Whenever you switch models in Antigravity, `agyline` dynamically tracks and renders the relevant quota bucket without requiring any theme reconfiguration.

assistant 2026-08-17 04:35:08
**Yes, exactly:**

```
model contains "gemini"  =>  gemini-*
else                     =>  3p-*
```

If neither `model.id` nor `model.display_name` contains `"gemini"` (case-insensitive), it is treated as a third-party model and `agyline` automatically selects the **`3p-*`** quota pools (`3p-5h`, `3p-weekly`). If either contains `"gemini"`, it selects **`gemini-*`** (`gemini-5h`, `gemini-weekly`).

user 2026-08-17 04:43:40
how does Quota differ from Usage (7d) ?

assistant 2026-08-17 04:43:40
Both components read from Antigravity's weekly quota buckets (`gemini-weekly` or `3p-weekly`), but they differ in formatting, labeling, and configuration options:

---

### Comparison

| Feature | **`Usage (7d)`** (`usage_seven_day`) | **`Quota`** (`quota`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Default Display** | `7d 55.4%` | `weekly 55%` (or `3p-weekly 66%`) |
| **Label Style** | Fixed standard prefix `7d` (pairs with `5h`) | Dynamic bucket name (e.g. `weekly`, `3p-weekly`) |
| **Precision** | Formats up to 1 decimal place (e.g. `55.4%`) | Formats rounded integer percentage (e.g. `55%`) |
| **Value Mode** | Configurable: **Remaining** vs **Used** (inverts percentage to show consumption) | Always shows **Remaining** percentage |
| **Bucket Selection** | Automatically selects weekly bucket for the active model | Automatically selects active model bucket or allows picking a specific custom bucket name |

---

### In Practice

- **Use `Usage (7d)`** if you want the classic statusline pair alongside **`Usage (5h)`** (e.g., `5h 8.6% | 7d 44.5%` or `5h 91.4% | 7d 55.5%`).
- **Use `Quota`** if you prefer Antigravity's bucket naming style (e.g., `weekly 55%`).

## 4. Model Knowledge
- **Antigravity Quota Structure**:
  - `input.quota` is a `HashMap<String, QuotaBucket>` containing keys like `"gemini-5h"`, `"gemini-weekly"`, `"3p-5h"`, `"3p-weekly"`.
  - `QuotaBucket` contains `remaining_fraction: Option<f64>`, `reset_time: Option<String>`, `reset_in_seconds: Option<u64>`.
- **Active Model Quota Routing**:
  - If model name/id does not contain "gemini", `FiveHourUsageComponent` uses `3p-5h` and `SevenDayUsageComponent` uses `3p-weekly`.
  - Otherwise, they use `gemini-5h` and `gemini-weekly`.
- **Component ID Stability**:
  - `ALL` in `src/config/types.rs` defines the order of components in TUI editor and default theme.

456:     pub fn add_missing_components(&mut self) {
457:         let defaults = Self::default_theme().components;

460:             if self.get_component(default.id).is_some() {
461:                 continue;
462:             }

465:                 .iter()

200: fn list_theme_files(dir: &Path) -> std::io::Result<Vec<(String, PathBuf)>> {
201:     if !dir.exists() {
202:         return Ok(Vec::new());
203:     }
204:     let mut themes = Vec::new();
205:     for entry in fs::read_dir(dir)? {
206:         let entry = entry?;
207:         let path = entry.path();
208:         if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) == Some("toml")
209:             && let Some(name) = path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str())
210:         {
211:             themes.push((name.to_string(), path));
212:         }
213:     }
214:     themes.sort_by_key(|(name, _)| name.to_lowercase());
215:     Ok(themes)
216: }
217:

221:     let mut theme: UserTheme = toml::from_str(&content).map_err(LoadError::Parse)?;

+/// What effort level indicator to display for the model component.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum ModelEffort {
+    #[default]
+    Show,
+    ThirdParty,
+    Hide,
+}
+
+impl ModelEffort {
+    pub fn display_name(self) -> &'static str {
+        match self {
+            Self::Show => "Show",
+            Self::ThirdParty => "Third Party",
+            Self::Hide => "Hide",
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
+        match self {
+            Self::Show => "show",
+            Self::ThirdParty => "third_party",
+            Self::Hide => "hide",
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub fn toggled(self) -> Self {
+        match self {
+            Self::Show => Self::ThirdParty,
+            Self::ThirdParty => Self::Hide,
+            Self::Hide => Self::Show,
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub fn from_options(options: &HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>) -> Self {
+        if let Some(val) = options.get(MODEL_OPTION_SHOW_EFFORT) {
+            if let Some(b) = val.as_bool() {
+                return if b { Self::Show } else { Self::Hide };
+            }
+            if let Some(s) = val.as_str() {
+                return match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
+                    "show" | "yes" | "true" => Self::Show,
+                    "third_party" | "thirdparty" | "3p" | "3p_only" | "third_party_only" => {
+                        Self::ThirdParty
+                    }
+                    "hide" | "no" | "false" => Self::Hide,
+                    _ => Self::default(),
+                };
+            }
+        }
+        Self::default()
+    }
+
+    pub fn should_display(self, is_third_party: bool) -> bool {
+        match self {
+            Self::Show => true,
+            Self::ThirdParty => is_third_party,
+            Self::Hide => false,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl fmt::Display for ModelEffort {
+    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
+        f.write_str(self.display_name())
+    }
+}
